eintraege.titel: Ten winning trades can die in one afternoon.
eintraege.text:
Ten winning trades can die in one afternoon.

He risked 1 % a trade and won ten in a row. Plus 10 %. Then one setup felt certain, so he risked 10 % on that one. It lost. Ten winners, erased by a single trade.

The size is the part you control before the trade. The outcome is the part you never did.

Send this to the friend who sizes up when he feels sure.

Have you ever sized up on a setup that felt certain? 👇

eintraege.titel: He won 7 trades out of 10 and still lost money.
eintraege.text:
He won 7 trades out of 10 and still lost money.

Seven winners at $40 is $280. Three losers at $180 is $540. That is minus $26 on every trade he takes. To break even at that ratio he needed more than 8 winners out of 10.

He left the win rate alone and cut the average loss to $60. The same 7 out of 10 turned into plus $10 a trade.

Send this to the friend who posts his win rate and never his average loss.

What is your average loss? 👇

eintraege.titel: Zero commission still has a cost.
eintraege.text:
Zero commission still has a cost.

Every market order pays the spread. Call it 0.1 % going in and 0.1 % coming out, so 0.2 % a round trip. If your average winner is 0.8 %, a quarter of every winner is gone before you count it.

The fee you can see is rarely the one that hurts.

Send this to the friend who picked his broker because the trades were free.

What spread do you actually pay? 👇

eintraege.titel: The second loss is never about the chart.
eintraege.text:
The second loss is never about the chart.

He lost 2 %. Then he wanted it back in one trade, so he doubled the size. That one lost 4 %. Down 2 % and then 4 % leaves him needing +6.3 % just to get back to where he woke up.

The first loss was the trade. The second one was the mood.

Send this to the friend who always takes one more after a red morning.

How long do you wait after a loss? 👇

eintraege.titel: Ask a trader about last month and he names three trades. Two of them worked.
eintraege.text:
Ask a trader about last month and he names three trades. Two of them worked.

The record says he took 41. The three he remembers are the ones with a story attached, and a story attaches itself to the ones that moved. The other 38 left nothing behind to remember them by.

Memory keeps the story. The record keeps the count.

Send this to the friend who says his last month was fine.

How many trades did you take last month, without looking? 👇

eintraege.titel: He halved his stop to risk less. He got stopped out twice as often.
eintraege.text:
He halved his stop to risk less. He got stopped out twice as often.

The position size stayed the same, so the stop moved closer to the entry and landed inside the daily noise. Less money leaves on each loss. More trades reach the stop at all. Both of those are risk, and only one of them is on the screen.

A stop has two dimensions. Most people only tune one.

Send this to the friend who keeps tightening after a red day.

Where does your stop actually sit, in noise or in structure? 👇

eintraege.titel: He won 90 of his last 100 trades and the account is down.
eintraege.text:
He won 90 of his last 100 trades and the account is down.

90 wins at 1R is plus 90R. 10 losses at 10R is minus 100R. He is sitting at minus 10R with a 90 % hit rate, and every one of those 90 winners was real.

A win rate without the ratio beside it describes nothing at all. The same arithmetic is what ends most prop firm challenges.
